samuel1.26.p1.b1.text: Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, opposite Jeshimon?

samuel1.26.p1.b2.text: So Saul, accompanied by three thousand chosen men of Israel, went down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David there.

samuel1.26.p1.b3.text: David was living in the wilderness. When he realized that Saul had followed him there, David sent out spies…

samuel1.26.p2.b1.text: Then David set out and went to the place where Saul had camped. He saw the place where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the general of his army, had lain down. Saul was lying inside the inner circle of the camp, with the troops camped around him.

samuel1.26.p2.b2.text: Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp?

samuel1.26.p3.b1.text: That night David and Abishai came to the troops…

samuel1.26.p3.b2.text: Saul was lying there asleep in the inner circle of the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. And Abner and the troops were lying around him.

samuel1.26.p3.b3.text: Today God has delivered your enemy into your hand. Now, therefore, please let me…with one stroke. I will not need to strike him twice!

samuel1.26.p4.b1.text: Do not destroy him, for who can lift a hand against the LORD’s anointed and be guiltless?

samuel1.26.p4.b2.text: As surely as the LORD lives, the LORD Himself will strike him down; either his day will come and he will die, or he will go into battle and perish…

samuel1.26.p4.b3.text: Instead, take the spear and water jug by his head, and let us go.

samuel1.26.p4.b4.text: …No one saw them or knew about it, nor did anyone wake up; they all remained asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.

samuel1.26.p5.b1.text: Then David crossed to the other side and stood atop the mountain at a distance; there was a wide gulf between them.

samuel1.26.p5.b2.text: Will you not answer me, Abner?

samuel1.26.p5.b4.text: …all of you deserve to die, since you did not protect your lord, the LORD’s anointed. Now look around. Where are the king’s spear and water jug that were by his head?

samuel1.26.p6.b1.text: Is that your voice, David my son?

samuel1.26.p6.b2.text: It is my voice, my lord and king,…What have I done? What evil is in my hand?

samuel1.26.p6.b3.text: So do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the presence of the LORD. For the king of Israel has come out to look for a flea, like one who hunts a partridge in the mountains.

samuel1.26.p7.b1.text: I have sinned. Come back, David my son…I have played the fool and have committed a grave error!

samuel1.26.p7.b2.text: Here is the king’s spear,…Let one of the young men come over and get it.

samuel1.26.p7.b3.text: For the LORD delivered you into my hand today, but I would not stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed.

samuel1.26.p7.b4.text: As surely as I valued your life today, so may the LORD value my life and rescue me from all trouble.

samuel1.26.p8.b1.text: May you be blessed, David my son. You will accomplish great things and will surely prevail.

samuel1.26.p8.b2.text: So David went on his way, and Saul returned home.
